summary: This is a reference page for the GETBIT function, which takes an INTEGER expression and a bit position and returns the value (0 or 1) of that bit. Bit positions run from 0 for the least significant bit up to 127 for the most significant bit. The page includes a syntax block, argument and return descriptions, and one example that retrieves bits at positions 100, 3, 2, 1 and 0 of the integer 11, showing 0, 1, 0, 1, 1 respectively.
one_line: Reference page for the GETBIT SQL function, which returns the 0 or 1 value of a given bit position in an integer.
key_facts: GETBIT returns the value of a bit at a specified position in a given INTEGER value.
The integer_expr argument must evaluate to a data type that can be cast to INTEGER.
bit_position starts at 0 for the least significant bit.
bit_position goes up to 127 for the most significant bit.
The function returns 0 or 1 as the value of the bit at the specified position.
The example runs SELECT GETBIT(11, 100), GETBIT(11, 3), GETBIT(11, 2), GETBIT(11, 1), GETBIT(11, 0).
The page is listed under the Language setting English.
